sentences.text: Mosasaurus was a derived mosasaur characterized by advanced evolutionary traits including a fully aquatic lifestyle. The skull of Mosasaurus is conical and tapers to a short snout that extends slightly beyond the frontmost teeth.
Mosasaurus teeth were specialized for cutting prey and featured highly prismatic surfaces with two opposite cutting edges.
A nearly complete Mosasaurus skeleton (SDSM 452) possessed seven cervical vertebrae, thirty-eight dorsal vertebrae, eight pygal vertebrae, and sixty-eight caudal vertebrae.
The name Mosasaurus refers to the fact that the first specimen was found near the Meuse River.
Researchers once estimated that the jaw length of M. hoffmanni was one-tenth of its total body length.
Using a smaller partial jaw, another study estimated the maximum length of M. hoffmanni to be 17.6 meters.
Only two Mosasaurus specimens with stomach contents are known, including a 75-million-year-old M. missouriensis containing dismembered remains of a 1-meter-long fish.
A subadult M. hoffmanni skeleton nicknamed "Lars" was recovered near Maastricht and contains acid-corroded bones of a juvenile turtle and other unidentified animals in its gut region.

The first fossils of Mosasaurus were discovered as skulls in a chalk quarry near Maastricht, Netherlands, in the late 18th century. The first known Mosasaurus fossil, a skull discovered in 1764 near Maastricht, was initially misidentified as a whale.
A fossil skeleton identified as a 49-foot-long fish was discovered by the Lewis and Clark Expedition in 1804 near the Missouri River.
Ambiguity in defining the genus Mosasaurus arose because 19th-century scientists did not provide a proper diagnosis during initial descriptions due to undefined nomenclatural rules.
Mosasaurus used its tail for swimming. Hermann Schlegel demonstrated in 1854 that Mosasaurus possessed fully aquatic flippers rather than limbs for walking.
Large scleral rings in Mosasaurus eye sockets suggest the animal had good vision.
Mosasaurus was likely not a scavenger because it had a poor sense of smell.
Fossil evidence documents an instance of the mosasaur Tylosaurus attacking a Mosasaurus.
A partial M. conodon skeleton shows multiple cuts, breaks, punctures, and a tooth piercing the quadrate bone, indicating attacks from another M. conodon.
Mosasaurus constantly shed teeth through a process where a replacement tooth developed inside the root of the original tooth and pushed it out.
Some M. hoffmanni jaws show evidence of infectious diseases caused by physical injuries.
Microanatomical studies show that juvenile Mosasaurus bone structures are comparable to those of adults.
Lingham-Soliar studied the head musculature of Mosasaurus hoffmanni in 1995.
Experts believe Mosasaurus lived near the ocean surface, feeding on fish, turtles, ammonites, and possibly smaller mosasaurs.
Recent 2024 research suggests that ambush predation may not have been the only hunting strategy for Mosasaurus hoffmanni.
Mosasaurus is the type genus of the family Mosasauridae and subfamily Mosasaurinae, and is a member of the order Squamata.
More than fifty species were once attributed to the genus Mosasaurus.
Bell recognized Plotosaurus as a distinct genus in his 1997 study despite finding it closely related to Mosasaurus.
The taxonomic validity of M. lemonnieri has been the subject of long-standing debate.
Fossil evidence indicates Mosasaurus inhabited much of the Atlantic Ocean and adjacent seaways.

Mosasaurus fossils have been found in the Midwest and East Coast of the US, Canada, Europe, Turkey, Russia, the Levant, the African coastline from Morocco to South Africa, Brazil, Argentina, and Antarctica.
Mosasaurus lived in the Mediterranean Tethys region, which covered modern-day Europe, Africa, and the Middle East during the Maastrichtian stage.
Mosasaurus and Prognathodon were the dominant and ecologically diversified mosasaur taxa throughout the Mediterranean Tethys seaway.
The appearance of Mosasaurus species at 79.5 Ma caused a complete faunal turnover in the Western Interior Seaway, profoundly restructuring marine ecosystems.
Scientists continue to debate whether the closest living relatives of Mosasaurus are monitor lizards or snakes.
